body:
Split out of T14. The findings ledger defaults to `.adlc/findings.jsonl` INSIDE the reviewed repository, so every component of that path is attacker-controlled. Hardening it drew a symlink finding in FOUR consecutive adversarial-review rounds (branch feat/reliability-port), each patch covering exactly the one component the previous review named. This ticket replaces the whole piecemeal approach with a single correct mechanism and gets it reviewed in isolation, with the full case matrix specified UP FRONT so a review cannot discover case N+1 one round at a time.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE OSCILLATION. Every prior fix was check-then-act on one path component at a time, with a different mechanism per component (O_NOFOLLOW for the leaf, lstat for parents). That is structurally incapable of being complete: it always leaves the next component or the next platform uncovered.

THREAT MODEL (bounded, stated so the review does not re-derive it). The reviewed repository is static files on disk. There is no attacker process running concurrently during a read-only review, so the threat is STATICALLY PLANTED symlinks anywhere in the ledger path — leaf, parent, or higher — pointing outside the repository. The attack goals are (a) redirect our JSON append to a victim file (corruption), and (b) redirect our 0600 chmod to a victim file (permission change). Live TOCTOU races require a concurrent attacker process that this model excludes; they are documented as out of scope, not chased.

CORRECT DESIGN — canonicalize, contain, open. One mechanism over the whole path:
1. root = fs.realpathSync(base) where base defaults to the working directory. realpath canonicalizes (/var -> /private/var on macOS), so containment is compared canonical-to-canonical. This is the CORRECT fix for the false positive that an earlier 'bounded walk' hacked around.
2. Ensure the parent exists: fs.mkdirSync(parent, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 }). mkdir never creates a symlink, and creating through an existing symlinked parent is caught by step 4.
3. realParent = fs.realpathSync(parent). This resolves EVERY symlink in the parent chain in one call.
4. Containment: refuse unless realParent === root or realParent starts with root + path.sep. A parent symlink that escapes the root is rejected; one that resolves to somewhere still inside the root is harmless.
5. Open the leaf INSIDE the canonical parent: fs.openSync(path.join(realParent, path.basename(ledgerPath)), O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND | O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600). O_NOFOLLOW refuses a leaf symlink atomically on POSIX.
6. Windows has no O_NOFOLLOW (constant is 0), so add ONE portable fs.lstatSync leaf check as a backstop before the open. Residual leaf TOCTOU on Windows is out of the static threat model.
7. Every subsequent operation (write, fstat, fchmod) goes through the returned fd, never the path, so nothing can be swapped after the open.

This DELETES assertNoSymlinkedParents, the bounded directory walk, the per-loop leaf check, and the O_NOFOLLOW-only leaf handling — all replaced by canonicalize->contain->open.

PACKAGING. Put the primitive in its own module src/safe-fs.js (e.g. openContainedAppendFd(targetPath, { base })), so it is reviewable in isolation and reusable. findings-ledger.js calls it and keeps only the ledger-specific concerns (JSONL serialization, the fchmod-existing hardening on the fd, best-effort semantics).

DEPENDS ON / RELATIONSHIP TO #34. The reliability PR (#34) is being descoped to the minimal, never-flagged T14 ledger behaviour (create new files 0600 via open-mode; no chmod-of-existing; no symlink logic), which is no worse than main. This ticket delivers the complete symlink safety separately. Do not re-add symlink logic to #34.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (the full matrix, specified up front):
- AC1: leaf symlink pointing outside the repo is refused; the victim file is neither written nor chmod-ed. VERIFY: unit test asserts a throw and asserts victim contents + mode unchanged.
- AC2: parent directory symlink (.adlc -> outside) is refused; victim unchanged. VERIFY: unit test.
- AC3: grandparent symlink (a component two levels up -> outside) is refused. VERIFY: unit test.
- AC4: a symlink that resolves to a location STILL INSIDE the repo root is allowed (no escape, no victim). VERIFY: unit test asserts the write succeeds at the resolved location.
- AC5: a canonical base under a symlinked prefix (simulate /var -> /private/var by placing base under a symlinked dir) produces NO false positive; a normal nested write succeeds. VERIFY: unit test with a symlinked ancestor of base.
- AC6: first write when the leaf does not yet exist creates it 0600 with no symlink present. VERIFY: unit test asserts creation + mode.
- AC7: an existing regular-file ledger is appended to and, if its mode is looser than 0600, tightened via fchmod on the fd (not the path). VERIFY: unit test with a pre-existing 0644 regular file.
- AC8: on win32 the portable lstat leaf check still refuses a leaf symlink even though O_NOFOLLOW is 0. VERIFY: unit test injecting platform + a symlinked leaf (skip on real win32 if symlink creation is unprivileged; otherwise run).
- AC9: the old helpers (assertNoSymlinkedParents and the bounded walk) are gone. VERIFY: grep in a test asserts they are not present in findings-ledger.js.
- AC10: full suite green, and an adversarial-review pass over this branch in isolation returns no gating symlink finding.
- AC11: TOCTOU / concurrent-attacker races are explicitly documented as out of the static threat model in src/safe-fs.js. VERIFY: the module says so and a test asserts the doc note exists.
title: Symlink-safe ledger writes: canonicalize-contain-open, spec-first and reviewed in isolation
